spec.name: Ironforge Dwarf Blacksmith
spec.description: A stout, broad-shouldered Warcraft-style dwarf smith with a braided ginger beard, standing at a tree-stump anvil and hammering a glowing bar held in tongs.
spec.layout: Blizzard/Warcraft stylisation: chunky, exaggerated, hand-painted-looking flat colours with bold faceted shapes. The dwarf is about 1.5 m tall with short legs (hip at y 0.58), a barrel chest and huge pauldrons. Hands and boots are oversized. The head is large (about 0.3 m wide) and sits almost directly on the shoulders. A heavy ginger beard with two braids falls over the chest. He stands at the origin, faces +Z, and his back is at about z -0.28. In front of him, centred at z 0.6, is a tree-stump anvil block (stump to y 0.42, anvil face at y 0.76, long axis along X, horn pointing to the model's left, +X). His right hand (-X side) holds a hammer that hovers over the anvil face. His left hand (+X side) holds long tongs gripping the end of a white-orange glowing bar lying on the anvil along X. A few sparks hover above the bar. Colour is zoned by place: Ironforge blue cloth with gold trim at the shoulders, bronze and steel plates with gold rivets, brown leather apron, belt and boots, brick-red shirt, ruddy skin, soot-dark iron. Every wear mark is its own small part: soot smudges on the apron, rivet rows, gold edge strips, scuffs on the toes. Warm colours sit on top and cool dark colours below. Rest pose: legs straight and slightly apart, arms forward and outward over the anvil with hands apart, jaw closed.

parts.builds: Hips, legs, boots and belt. Pelvis and short stocky legs of heavy trousers in leatherDark and clothBlueDark, with thick thighs and calves built as sweeps on the hip, knee and ankle joints. Big chunky boots in leather, with a leatherDark sole slab, a toe cap and heel block, a steel-trimmed cuff with a gold buckle on each side, and scuffs and soot patches as small parts. Fold-over bronze knee pads with rivets. Wide belt around the waist (y 0.62-0.72) in leatherDark with a big gold-framed bronze buckle in front, rivet studs, and small pouches at the sides. A hanging leather apron skirt flap in front, from the belt down to y 0.28 at z about 0.23, with a gold edge stitch strip, soot smudges and a scorch-mark hem, and a hammer loop and tong loop on the left hip. Cloth tassels in clothBlue at the belt sides. Every piece is bold and faceted. Pieces ride hips, hipL/R, kneeL/R, ankleL/R and toeL/R.
parts.attaches: The belt top meets the torso at waistTop (y 0.7). The hip joints sit at hips, and the apron's upper edge is covered by the torso's bib at the belt. Boots rest on the floor at bootL and bootR.

parts.builds: Chest, back, shoulders and neck. A big barrel chest and a short thick neck, in a brick-red shirt (shirt) with rolled sleeve cuffs, built as a loft or sweep on spine and chest. A leather apron bib on the front, from waistTop up to the upper chest, in leather with gold-trimmed straps over the shoulders. It carries rivet rows, a stitched seam, a tool pocket and soot smudges, and a sooty chest plate patch in leatherDark. Huge layered pauldrons on both shoulders, with a bronze plate base, a steel upper plate, and a gold rim strip. Each has a clothBlue cloth mantle drape with a clothBlueDark trim and a row of gold rivets, and a small gold rune emblem on the front. A thick leather collar at the neckBase with a bronze clasp. At the back, a leather tool roll and satchel (y 0.85-1.1, z down to -0.28) with straps in leatherDark, buckles in gold and a hammer-head handle sticking out. The torso's back and sides stay inside z -0.28 to 0.26.
parts.attaches: Starts at waistTop, ending flush with the belt. The neck ends at neckBase, where the head part takes over, and the beard hangs over the bib at z 0.27 to 0.31. The shoulder pauldrons cover the top of the arm sweeps at shoulderL/R (the arms part starts there). Chest front at z 0.21.

parts.builds: The head and beard, the signature piece, built big and with the most care. The head is about 0.3 m wide and 0.3 m tall, centred at headCenter, in ruddy skin on the head bone: a broad cranium, heavy brow ridge, wide cheekbones with skinShade cheek blush, ears on the sides with gold hoop earrings, a big bulbous nose, and skinShade lips. Two big eyes in eyeWhite with eyeIris irises, dark pupils and a small white highlight, set under bushy beardDark brows that angle down toward the nose. Hair is a ginger topknot with a gold clasp, plus thick sideburns that run into the beard. Bronze-rimmed goggles are pushed up on the forehead, with steel lenses and a leatherDark strap around the head. A thick walrus moustache in beard colours sweeps out left and right with curled tips. The beard is a big solid mass in beard, running from the cheeks and chin down over the chest to beardTip (y 0.8, z 0.27), with overlapping broad blades in a beardDark root, beard and beardLight tip palette. The beard is wide at the top, and two long braids hang from it in front with gold ring clasps and tips tied with leather. The mouth is built as a separate upper part (on the head bone) and a lower jaw on the jaw bone, with a visible dark mouth gap in beardDark/skinShade; the chin and the main beard mass ride the jaw. Nothing sits in front of the face except the moustache and beard below it.
parts.attaches: The neck base is at neckBase (y 1.12), and the head bone sits at the neck top. The beard hangs over the torso bib to beardTip, in front of the chest (chest front z 0.21), with its lowest braid tips at about y 0.76, above the belt. The goggles and topknot sit on top and nothing else is mounted on the head.

parts.builds: Both arms, the hammer and the tongs. Thick muscular arms built as sweeps on the chains shoulderL/elbowL/wristL and shoulderR/elbowR/wristR, with rolled brick-red sleeves on the upper arms, bare ruddy skin forearms with skinShade shading, heavy leather bracers with bronze rivets and gold edge strips, and soot smudges. Chunky oversized gloved hands in leather at each wrist: a fist block, a thumb, and four finger blocks wrapped around the tool, with leatherDark stitching lines. Right hand (-X side) grips a smith's hammer: a wooden handle (wood, with a woodDark wrap and a leather end cap) running from behind the fist to the head, and a big square steel hammer head at hammerHead with a bronze band, a steelDark face and a gold rivet; the handle is about 0.45 m long, and the head hovers about 0.12 m above the anvil face. Left hand (+X side) grips long iron tongs: two iron handles with leather grips running from wristL forward and down to tongGrip, a bronze pivot rivet, and flat iron jaws holding the end of the glowing workpiece at tongGrip (the bar itself belongs to the anvil part). The arms are extended forward and out in a readable rest pose, with hands apart.
parts.attaches: Arm roots at shoulderL/R, under the torso's pauldrons. Hands at wristL/R. The hammer head sits at hammerHead, above anvilTop. The tong jaws reach tongGrip on the workpiece end (workpieceEnd is x 0.44, so grip at x 0.4).

parts.builds: The tree-stump block, the anvil and the hot work. A thick tree-stump block (wood, radius about 0.27, y 0 to 0.42, centred stumpCenter) with faceted bark ridges in woodDark, root flares at the base that dip slightly into the floor, a lighter top ring surface with growth-ring lines, deep axe-cut notches, and two steel hoops with rivets near the top and base. On it sits a big blacksmith's anvil in iron and steelDark: base feet (y 0.42-0.5, x +/-0.2, z 0.5-0.7), a narrower waist (to y 0.64), and a body (y 0.64-0.76, x +/-0.36, z 0.49-0.71) with a polished steel face plate on top at anvilTop (y 0.76), a pointed conical horn tapering toward +X to x 0.66, a stepped heel with a hardy hole and a round pritchel hole at the back (-X, to x -0.46). It has bronze edge strips, gold rivet-like studs and soot, scorch and scuff marks on the face. On the face lies a glowing bar from workpieceStart (x -0.05) to workpieceEnd (x 0.44) at y 0.78, with a hotCore centre strip, a hotMid body and hotEdge cooled ends, using the glow kit (strength 1.5 to 2); the end at x 0.44 is held by the tongs at tongGrip. Small glowing sparks, in hotCore, hotMid and hotEdge, hang above the bar (below y 0.95). A few cooled slag chips and a chisel in iron are on the stump edge and the anvil's far side, away from the dwarf's hands.
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor at stumpCenter. The anvil top plate is at anvilTop (y 0.76) and the glowing bar spans workpieceStart to workpieceEnd. The tongs from the arms part grip its end at tongGrip, and the hammer head hovers above it at hammerHead.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith at his anvil—stout build, oversized shoulders, standing about 1.3m tall, facing forward with the anvil positioned in front of him. He'll have a hammer raised in one hand and tongs gripping a glowing workpiece in the other.

I'm leaning toward a slight A-pose with arms angled forward-outward about 45° over the anvil, hammer resting or poised in the right hand while the left holds tongs with the bar against the anvil face. Overall footprint comes to roughly 1.3m wide including arms and hammer, 1.45m tall accounting for a braided beard and helmet, with the anvil and stump positioned just in front of the dwarf's body—keeping extra props minimal rather than adding a full forge setup.

I'm splitting the model into five parts: lower body (boots, legs, apron, belt, hip joints), torso (chest, apron upper, pauldrons, shoulders, spine), head (face, beard, helmet, jaw joint), arms (limb chains with hammer and tongs plus the heated bar), and the anvil assembly itself.

Now I'm working out proportions for a big stocky dwarf — feet at floor level, boots around 0.16 tall, hips at 0.55, torso spanning roughly 0.7 to 1.12 with wide shoulders near 1.05, and a short neck leading into the head, with the beard sitting in front of the chest down to about 0.75.

Head center around y=1.27 with the helmet pushing total height to about 1.5, and I'm placing the dwarf facing +Z with the anvil setup in front of him at roughly z=0.55 — figuring the stump height, anvil body height, and top plate so the anvil surface lands near his waist for a natural working pose.

I'm working through the anvil's orientation and placement — deciding the horn points sideways, sizing the face length and width, and centering it around z=0.6 so its span clears the dwarf's belly and beard, keeping enough gap for his arms to reach while fitting the whole stump-to-anvil span within about a meter depth.

Now I'm figuring out the arm geometry: placing shoulder joints symmetrically, setting upper arm and forearm lengths, and working out a resting pose where the right arm holds the hammer with its head touching down on the anvil's face.

I'm setting hand positions for the figure: right hand gripping the hammer, left hand holding tongs that grip the workpiece bar resting on the anvil face, and working out where the bar extends toward the center of the anvil.

Now I'm figuring out the hammer mount: head position near (-0.12,0.95,0.60) with the handle running from the hand grip to the head, checking the length comes out around 0.4 so it reads as a believable hammer, with the head hovering just above the anvil surface.

Then I'm working out arm joint positions—shoulders, elbows, and hands for both sides—checking segment lengths come out roughly equal (~0.28-0.29) so the arms look proportionate and symmetric.

Now I'm laying out the spine hierarchy: hips as root, then spine1, chest, neck, and head, adjusting their y-positions upward. I'm also placing the jaw joint near the head pivot for a hinge-like mouth movement.

Then I move to the limbs, planning joint chains for arms and legs before any parts are attached, naming them with simple alphanumeric labels like shoulderL, elbowL, wristL for arms, and hipL, kneeL, ankleL, footL for the legs, positioning them to fit a short dwarf-like stature.

I'll add a handL joint at the wrist tip with direction toward the grip, skipping finger joints except maybe thumb. For the right side I'll mirror with shoulderR, elbowR, wristR, keeping in mind the spec's convention that left is +X, so the hammer-holding arm sits on the negative-X side even though that's the model's right hand. I'm placing the anvil horn toward +X and the hammer near -X over the anvil face, with both wrists roughly at x ±0.33.

I'm now positioning the hammer head over the bar on the anvil, working out the handle-to-head geometry so the head hovers just above the bar's top surface with the cylinder axis oriented along the handle.

Now I'm fleshing out the anvil's full geometry: the stump cylinder as a base, then the anvil body stacked above it with a narrower waist, flared base, tapered horn extending to one side, and a heel with hardy hole on the other, calculating the top surface height so the bar sits correctly on it.

For the overall bounding box I'm reasoning through the x/y/z extents including the horn, shoulder width, and stump radius to settle on an approximate size of [1.25, 1.5, 1.12]. For the dwarf's head I'm thinking Warcraft Ironforge blacksmith style — bushy braided beard, heavy brows, big nose, maybe a leather cap or goggles.
